stories.headline: Ex-judges panel to examine Election Commission's SIR of electoral rolls
stories.title: Ex-judges panel to examine Election Commission's SIR of electoral rolls
stories.summary: Ex-judges panel to examine Election Commission's SIR of electoral rolls
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A lawyers' body has formed a panel of former judges to examine the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
The inquiry will test its legal validity and hear affected citizens before recommending changes.
A lawyers' association has set up a five-member panel of former Supreme Court and high court judges to examine the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll.

The Lawyers Association for Constitution (LAFC) said the panel will look into the constitutional and statutory validity, the methodology and the overall impact of the exercise to revise the voter list.
The panel will be headed by former Supreme Court judge Madan B Lokur.
LAFC said the commission will work independently and will also examine whether eligible citizens were kept on the electoral roll and whether ineligible entries were properly removed.

In a release, the association said, "The newly-formed independent commission of former judges on the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral roll will function with complete autonomy to examine the constitutional and statutory validity, methodology and overall impact of the SIR exercise on eligible voters."
Besides Lokur, the panel will include former Supreme Court judge.
A K Patnaik, former chief justice of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court Badar Durrez Ahmad and former judges Rekha Sharma and Anjana Prakash.
As part of its inquiry, the commission plans to hold public hearings across the country.
Full and regional benches will travel to different places to record the views and testimonies of affected citizens, civil society organisations and experts.
LAFC said the commission will have final responsibility for its findings and recommendations.
